title: CmdPal: renew extension foreground permission for each command
summary: The per-command foreground-permission design remains technically current, but open maintainer PR #50651 now implements it with focused regression tests and passing CI.

judgment.rationale: The prior design correctly identified that Command Palette treated extension identity as a proxy for a revocable Windows foreground grant. Since that evaluation, the issue author opened PR #50651, which explicitly closes #50642, moves foreground-grant logic into ExtensionWrapper, renews the grant for every command, preserves liveness checks when switching extensions, and adds unit coverage for repeated commands and extension transitions. A separate dashboard design or implementation would now duplicate active upstream work.
evidence: The complete issue report identifies PowerToysRootPageService.SetActiveExtension as granting foreground permission only when the extension identity changes.
Current main still contains that conditional and calls CoAllowSetForegroundWindow only inside the extension-change branch.
Open PR #50651 explicitly closes #50642 and changes SetActiveExtension to attempt a foreground grant on every command invocation.
PR #50651 adds IExtensionWrapper.TryAllowSetForeground and keeps the prior liveness lookup for extension changes while reusing the current extension object for consecutive commands.

PR #50651 adds PowerToysRootPageServiceTests covering three consecutive commands, switching command owners, returning to an earlier extension, GoHome, built-in commands, and both grant success and failure.
The current PR head caff2cb742171a2f3bf0580937b4583f2c331c32 has passing dependency, intake, telemetry, CLA, x64, arm64, Command Palette SDK, and aggregate PowerToys CI checks.
The issue author removed Needs-Author-Feedback after the PR was linked; no reporter evidence is currently requested.
judgment.recommended_action: Follow PR #50651 through upstream review and merge; do not start or approve a parallel design.

confidence.rationale: The issue author owns both the report and linked closing PR, and the implementation matches the previously proposed renewal boundary with focused tests and passing CI.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open upstream PR #50651 is a concrete implementation of the exact per-command foreground-permission renewal described by the issue and prior design.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette extension commands can lose the ability to activate a target window because the foreground grant is revocable, while current main renews it only when the active extension changes; a linked maintainer PR now implements per-command renewal.
known_information: The maintainer-authored report uses a Visual Studio development build identified as PowerToys 0.101.
The observed target application may flash in the taskbar or become visible without keyboard focus.
PowerToysRootPageService.OnPerformCommand calls SetActiveExtension for commands owned by a CommandPaletteHost.
Current main updates _activeExtension and calls CoAllowSetForegroundWindow only when the extension differs from the previously active extension.
Windows can revoke a foreground grant after input to another process or a later grant to another process.
Issue #39255 contains an earlier public reproduction of consecutive top-level commands and list-page commands losing foreground access.
Issue #50642 is assigned to its author, jiripolasek, and now has only Issue-Bug and Product-Command Palette labels.
Open PR #50651 is authored by the same maintainer, explicitly closes #50642, and is marked Ready for review.
PR #50651 is not a draft, has no reviews or inline discussion yet, and currently requires review.
All reported checks on PR head caff2cb742171a2f3bf0580937b4583f2c331c32 are complete and successful.
inferences: Renewing permission immediately before each extension command aligns the grant lifetime with the operation that consumes it.
Keeping the liveness check on extension transitions avoids adding the extra extension lookup to every repeated command while still attempting each foreground grant.
Because the linked PR implements the same control-flow boundary and regression cases as the prior design, the design is superseded by active implementation rather than invalidated.
Merge readiness still depends on upstream review despite passing CI.
issue_context.analysis: The new cross-reference is decisive. Before PR #50651, the issue justified an actionable design because the report named the failing conditional and the API lifetime mismatch. The linked PR now makes that exact change: SetActiveExtension atomically updates active identity and calls TryAllowSetForeground for every invocation; ExtensionWrapper owns the native call and error handling; tests assert repeated same-extension grants and state transitions. The issue therefore remains actionable only through the existing upstream PR. Pulse should not expose Approve design, Request information, Reproduce, or a status-only comment while the closing implementation is under review.
